A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed and validated a digital RT-PCR platform that can be used for quantifying DNA and RNA in volumes as small as 1 nL with 1,000, 5,000, or 10,000-fold dynamic range, and that is suitable for point-of-care applications.

we have demonstrated a new approach for digital PCR that can be applied to any platform, and we have demonstrated that the theory and software presented are useful for designing digital PCR experiments.

we have developed a theoretical framework and software for the design and analysis of MV digital PCR and dilution series, and have experimentally demonstrated that the design approach can be used to design devices for quantifying DNA or RNA with high dynamic range and resolution using a single SlipChip.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the theory and software presented in this paper are useful for designing and analyzing digital assays and dilution series in any platform.
multivolume designs can be used to simplify digital assays and enable high-throughput multiplexed assays with high dynamic range.
the number of wells required to achieve a given dynamic range and resolution in a digital assay can be greatly reduced using multivolume designs.
